sources.locator: Methods, Data collection; Results, Species occurrence: direct group observations in southern mainland Guinea-Bissau and Bijagós Archipelago during surveys 2015–2022; three groups at Cufada Lagoons Natural Park and three at Dulombi National Park in mangroves, primary and secondary forests, plus 12 groups at Boé National Park in woodland and herbaceous savanna. claims.text: During 2015–2022 surveys in southern mainland Guinea-Bissau and the Bijagós Archipelago, the authors directly observed 18 Chlorocebus sabaeus groups: three groups at Cufada Lagoons Natural Park and three at Dulombi National Park in mangroves, primary and secondary forests, and 12 at Boé National Park in woodland and herbaceous savanna. Separately, they reported 76 molecularly identified fecal samples from 11 geographically distinct locations in Cufada, Cantanhez, Dulombi, Boé and Ganogo island. These are study-site observations and samples, not a complete habitat or distribution assessment.
claims.locator: Methods, Data collection; Results, Species occurrence, paragraphs reporting 18 observed groups and 76 fecal samples; Methods, DNA amplification and sequencing, species assignment using mtDNA and BLAST.
claims.placeTimeScope: Southern mainland Guinea-Bissau: Cufada Lagoons Natural Park, Dulombi National Park, Boé National Park and Cantanhez Forest National Park; Bijagós Archipelago including Ganogo island. Direct group observations during surveys in 2015–2022; molecularly identified fecal samples were reported from fieldwork conducted between 2008 and 2022.
claims.lifeStatus: Free-ranging field observations and non-invasive fecal samples attributed to Chlorocebus sabaeus; captive and domesticated populations not assessed.

gaps: Evidence is bounded to surveyed sites in Guinea-Bissau and the reported survey/sample periods; it does not establish species-wide habitat preferences or a complete modern range.
The article also studies Cercopithecus campbelli; only species-specific Chlorocebus sabaeus data are used here.
No independent taxon-wide evolutionary synthesis was assessed; study-level mtDNA findings are outside this batch’s supported claim scope.
No complete geographic distribution or range boundary was assessed; local study records are not treated as a range assessment.
No fossil or paleontological search was performed.
No current formal conservation assessment, trend or threat category was verified.

reasons: One primary field study supports only bounded ecology observations in Guinea-Bissau.
Morphology, life history, evolution, distribution boundaries, fossils and current conservation status were not assessed.
Independent expert review and comprehensive multi-source coverage are incomplete.
